checks_run.procedure: The D-238 open questions. Look for a served column, response, notification channel or write path that still names a sensitive record, or a token sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden literal. Read: automation/versions.ts (literalPositions, mapLiteralsAt, redactConditionLiterals, resolveRestrictedTokens, updateVersion); automation/executions.ts and failures.ts (masking); dry-run.ts (served plan and keys); the action and starter parameter schemas; integrations/connectors.ts (checkFieldMappings, commitOnBehalfOf); secret-refs.ts; access/sensitive-reach.ts (restrictedIdsAmong, markedInOrganizations); tasks/deep-links.ts; and the worker's notifications.ts and digests.ts. Plus the token probes of SEC-R1-19.
checks_run.expected: No path discloses a hidden id or literal to a non-admitted reader, and no token sequence loses or misplaces a literal; or a finding.
checks_run.actual: No defect found, so no finding. Tokens: position k counts every literal of the STORED version in reading order, identically in redact and resolve (string, boolean and each `in` element; numbers cannot occur, since the schema allows only text, boolean and text arrays). The tag is HMAC(row key, id, row version), and the update resolves against the row locked FOR UPDATE after If-Match. Grant changes, concurrent saves and copies across rows or versions are refused or resolve to the same literal (P8/P13–P20 and t2/t3 pass, and the mutant is caught). A token can only be moved within conditions: action parameters are strict schemas (role codes, message key, uuid targetTransformationId) and starter parameters are numbers, so a token cannot reach a rendered or served field. The summary renders tokens as 'a restricted record'. Dry-run keys use the dry-run id, never a payload id. A dry-run is an equality-only oracle: eq, neq and in are exact matches, and gt..lte require decimals. It confirms a guessed uuidv7, but cannot extract one. Execution and failure texts are masked. Channel sends apply recipientCanRead before rendering, and digests are count-only inbox items. D-229: connector field_mappings.source (any text, 1–100 characters) and SecretRef names CAN contain a uuid. They are written only by connector administrators (connector.configure), or in IT's manifest, and are read by connector readers. They are administrator-authored configuration, in the same class as free text, not a stored reference the product creates. I accept the cannot-name classification. D-228 (4): markedInOrganizations covers every organization of the principal, and another organization's records are unreachable, so an id from another organization discloses nothing resolvable. Accepted.

checks_run.procedure: Direct review of the P6 diff 660f40c7d..98feb869c (877 product files; migrations 0098–0127), with the files read in full where security-relevant (list in the narrative). Plus a scan of P6-touched API files that open a transaction for refreshPrincipal and commit-time names, followed by reading the P6-new write paths.
checks_run.command: git diff 660f40c7d 98feb869c -- apps packages; see 35-commit-time-scan.log and the narrative
checks_run.expected: No exploitable defect in authorization, integrity, injection or secrets handling.
checks_run.actual:
Everything below holds; the one exception is F-DG6-920.
- Webhooks: HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.delivery.body with timingSafeEqual; the tolerance window; current and previous secret during the grace; one uniform 401; the body parsed only after the signature; strict UTF-8; replay answered by receipt, with 409 on a reused id with another body; the advisory lock plus a unique backstop; the 1 MiB body limit; the webhook rate class.
- XLSX: central-directory limits; ratio 100:1; inflate output capped at the declared size; CRC; no DTD, macro or external link; formulas reported as null, never their cached values.
- Exports: formula injection neutralised (packages/reporting injection.ts).
- Evidence preview: raster only, magic re-checked on every read, sandbox CSP, nosniff, CORP, no-store. Download is octet-stream attachment.
- Export download: re-checks the snapshot's restricted records on every download.
- Deep links: an opaque token, re-authorized on every resolution, with one uniform 403.
- Channel sends: outside transactions, under a session advisory lock, restricted messages redacted.
- Outbound writes: dispatch outside transactions under the same key, with replay detection.
- http_pull: redirect 'error', a 10 MiB cap, bearer credentials host-bound (F-DG6-181).
- OIDC: exact issuer, audience and azp checks, plus JWKS, nonce and PKCE.
- Rate limits: keyed by user or IP behind an explicit trustProxy list.
- Worker: batch 1–50 and concurrency 1–16 (bounded); the per-(version, trigger key) advisory lock with the automation_execution_once_key backstop.
- Ledger: the version at occurrence from 0122/0123 with the rule enabled now (D-204/D-205). The residual commit-order race is documented in ADR-0043; I accept it, since the action only ever runs for an enabled rule.
- Keyset cursors: every P6 list carries microsecond cursor keys (cursorInstant or to_char … .US), and webhook endpoints truncate both sides to milliseconds.
- Commit-time re-checks: the P6-new write paths re-read grants inside the transaction (automation configurer→refreshPrincipal after FOR UPDATE; webhooks recheckConfigure; outbound transaction 1; export cancel; deliverable confirmation openWrite atCommit).
- Observations, not findings: (1) A deliverable confirmation accepts any verified evidence of the deliverable's transformation and records it as the source (ADR-0055 §6 as designed). (2) commitOnBehalfOf may name any active user of the organization. The auto-commit is audited as actor 'service' with onBehalfOfUserId, and is re-authorized on that user's grants. (3) audit-events.test.ts:386 is a stale it.todo whose case is covered elsewhere.
